E1:
(1) Vending machine: a ProximityPrompt only shows when its parent gives it a world position: an Attachment, a BasePart, or a Model with a PrimaryPart. Its parent here is a Folder, and the Model above it has no PrimaryPart, so the prompt has no position and is never drawn. Fix: parent the prompt to an Attachment inside the front panel part, or to that part itself. Setting VendingMachine.PrimaryPart and parenting the prompt to the Model also works, but an Attachment lets you place it exactly.
(2) Lever: RequiresLineOfSight defaults to true, and the glass case is a separate part blocking the line of sight from the camera to the prompt. Fix any one of these: set prompt.RequiresLineOfSight = false; set the glass CanQuery = false (CanQuery only takes effect when CanCollide is false, so you may need to change that too); or move the prompt onto an Attachment outside the glass, in front of the case. Keep prompt stations about 20+ studs apart so prompts don't flicker. (Vault: World-Space UI; Lobby and Hub Design)
E2:
- AlwaysOnTop = false. When it is true the tag is drawn over all 3D geometry, which is why tags show through walls. When false, the tag is depth-tested and walls hide it.
- MaxDistance = 100. The default of 0 (or inf) means unlimited, so tags are visible across the map. Past MaxDistance the billboard is not drawn.
- Size: use Scale instead of Offset, e.g. UDim2.fromScale(4, 1). In a BillboardGui, Scale is measured in studs, so the tag acts like a world object and shrinks with distance. Offset is in pixels, so the tag stays a constant size on screen. Inside the scaled tag, use TextScaled with a UITextSizeConstraint so text stays readable.
- Optional: position the tag with StudsOffsetWorldSpace / ExtentsOffsetWorldSpace = (0, 1, 0) above the head. (Vault: World-Space UI - BillboardGui and SurfaceGui; Nametags and Overhead Bars)
E3:
With CharacterAutoLoads = false, the engine never spawns characters, not on join and not after death. The server must call LoadCharacterAsync() for every spawn (LoadCharacter is the deprecated 2026 name for the same thing). RespawnTime only applies to automatic loading, so it is ignored. Minimal server fix:
```lua
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
Players.CharacterAutoLoads = false
local function spawn(p)
  if p.Parent then pcall(p.LoadCharacterAsync, p) end
end
Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(function(p)
  p.CharacterAdded:Connect(function(char)
    char:WaitForChild("Humanoid").Died:Connect(function()
      task.delay(3, spawn, p) -- your own respawn delay
    end)
  end)
  spawn(p) -- or wait until the round starts
end)
```
Only the server can do this. Check player.Parent after the delay. pcall the call, because a single error means nobody spawns. LoadCharacterAsync yields and resets the Backpack and PlayerGui (unless ResetOnSpawn = false). Your round logic decides when to call spawn.
E4:
Raycasts skip any part with CanQuery = false. That is the whole purpose of CanQuery (it only takes effect when CanCollide is false, which is true here). So the glass does not exist to the laser, and no filter can bring it back. Fixes:
- Set glass CanQuery = true and keep CanCollide = false. Players can still walk through it, and rays now hit it. Then filter out other unwanted parts with RaycastParams (ExcludeInstances/IncludeInstances, or the older FilterDescendantsInstances + FilterType).
- Or put players and glass in collision groups that don't collide, keep the glass CanCollide = true and CanQuery = true, and give the laser's RaycastParams.CollisionGroup a group that collides with glass. (Vault: Collision and Physics Geometry; Raycasts Shapecasts and Spatial Queries)
E5:
Error 1: Clone() skips instances whose Archivable is false. When the root itself is non-archivable, Clone() returns nil, so g:PivotTo fails with "attempt to index nil". Fix: set template.Archivable = true (fix or remove the plugin), or set it to true just before cloning.
Error 2: Destroy() sets Parent to nil and locks the Parent property permanently, and disconnects connections. A destroyed instance can never be reparented, so the 'reuse the template' plan breaks on the second spawn. It also destroys your only template.
Correct pattern: keep a never-parented, Archivable template in ServerStorage/ReplicatedStorage. Clone it for every spawn, and Destroy the clone when it dies (or Debris:AddItem it).
```lua
local template = game.ServerStorage.Enemies.Goblin
template.Archivable = true
local function spawnGoblin(cf)
  local g = template:Clone()
  g:PivotTo(cf)
  g.Parent = workspace
  g.Humanoid.Died:Once(function() task.delay(2, g.Destroy, g) end)
  return g
end
```
If you need reuse for performance, pool clones by parenting them to nil or to storage. Never Destroy a clone you plan to reuse.

```lua
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local SIZE = Vector3.new(6, 5, 6)
local function swing(attacker: Model)
  local root = attacker:FindFirstChild("HumanoidRootPart")
  if not root then return end
  local params = OverlapParams.new()
  params.FilterType = Enum.RaycastFilterType.Exclude
  params.FilterDescendantsInstances = {attacker}
  local cf = root.CFrame * CFrame.new(0, 0, -3)
  local hit = {}
  for _, part in workspace:GetPartBoundsInBox(cf, SIZE, params) do
    local char = part:FindFirstAncestorOfClass("Model")
    local hum = char and char:FindFirstChildOfClass("Humanoid")
    if hum and not hit[char] and hum.Health > 0 then
      hit[char] = true -- once per swing, not once per limb
      hum:TakeDamage(20)
    end
  end
end
```
Run this on the server when a validated swing request arrives, with a cooldown check. (The 2026 params.ExcludeInstances = {attacker} works too.) Caveat: GetPartBoundsInBox tests each part's axis-aligned bounding box, not its real geometry, so large or rotated parts and meshes can count as hits when they are only near the box. For exact overlap, use GetPartsInPart with a box part, at a higher cost. Lag also means the server sees positions slightly behind the client.

Simplest approach: set the model's pivot to the trunk base once in Studio. Then PivotTo(CFrame.new(result.Position) * yaw) is enough, and ScaleTo (which scales around the pivot) keeps the tree grounded.
Avoid these older approaches:
- SetPrimaryPartCFrame / GetPrimaryPartCFrame. They need a PrimaryPart (this model has none), are deprecated, and drift over time. PivotTo/GetPivot work without a PrimaryPart.
- Resizing each part's Size and Position by hand. It is error-prone, breaks welds, joints, attachments and meshes, and doesn't scale effects. Model:ScaleTo scales all of this consistently and records the scale (GetScale).

E11:
Use MemoryStoreService for both. It is in-memory, cross-server and low-latency.
- Matchmaking queue: MemoryStoreQueue. Use AddAsync to add a ticket, ReadAsync with an invisibility timeout to claim tickets, then RemoveAsync before the timeout ends so the claim can't be read twice. A server pairs two tickets and uses TeleportService to send both players to a reserved server. Check Roblox's built-in matchmaking first.
- Hourly top 100: MemoryStoreSortedMap. Use the score as the sort key, and UpdateAsync to keep only the best score per player. Read with GetRangeAsync (max 200 items per call). Use a key per hour, e.g. 'scores_2026102914', with an expiration of a bit over 1 hour, so the board resets by itself. Every item needs an expiration, max 45 days.
Limits that shape the design:
- Memory quota: 64 KB + 1.2 KB x users.
- Requests: 1,000 + 120 x CCU per minute, shared by the whole experience. Each item returned by a range read costs one unit, so don't poll the top 100 from every server every few seconds. Cache it and read it every 30-60 s.
- Value size: max 32 KB.
- Per structure: 1,000,000 items / 100 MB.
- A single map or queue lives on one partition (about 30k units/min), so shard hot structures.
Use DataStores only to keep data permanently, such as an all-time board in OrderedDataStore.
E12:
Per-server budgets (legacy per-server defaults, which still apply):
- GetAsync: 60 + 40 x players per minute.
- Set/Update/Remove writes: 60 + 40 x players per minute.
- With 40 players that is 1,660/min each.
- Each request type has a 30-request queue. Overflow raises errors 301-306.
- UpdateAsync counts against both read and write budgets.
Since 2026 there are also per-experience limits, shared with Open Cloud:
- Read: 300 + 40 x CCU per minute.
- Write: 300 + 20 x CCU per minute.
- List: 300 + 2 x CCU per minute.
- Remove: 300 + 40 x CCU per minute.
These are now the binding ones.
Your load: 40 autosaves per 60 s is about 40 writes/min plus leave saves, which is well within budget.
Per-key limits:
- Value size: max 4,194,304 characters (4 MB) after JSON serialization.
- Throughput: per-key 25 MB/min read and 4 MB/min write.
- Keep writes to one key several seconds apart; the classic rule is no more than one write per ~6 s. A leave-save right after an autosave can be throttled, so skip the autosave if one ran recently, or coalesce them.
- Key, store name and scope: max 50 characters each.
Design tips:
- Check budgets with GetRequestBudgetForRequestType before bulk work.
- pcall and retry with backoff.
- Save on BindToClose.

E14:
- External call: the bot sends an HTTPS POST to Open Cloud MessagingService. The endpoint is https://apis.roblox.com/messaging-service/v1/universes/{universeId}/topics/{topic}, with a JSON body {"message": "..."} (a string, about 1 KB max).
- Credentials: create an Open Cloud API key in the Creator Dashboard. Give it only the messaging-service publish permission for this one experience, and restrict it to the bot server's IP. Send it in the x-api-key header. Keep it in the bot's secrets, never in game code.
- In-game: each server calls MessagingService:SubscribeAsync("Announcements", function(msg) ... end) at startup, wrapped in pcall with retry. msg.Data holds the text and msg.Sent the timestamp. The handler validates the message, then fires a RemoteEvent:FireAllClients to show the banner. Messages usually arrive in well under a second, but delivery is best-effort: no guaranteed delivery or order.
- If the announcement must reach servers that start later, also write it to a DataStore or MemoryStore that new servers read at boot.
- Limits: a receive budget of about 40 + 80 x servers per minute per topic, and subscriptions per server of 20 + 8 x players. One topic and rare publishes are fine.
- Filter or authorize text on the bot side, because it is shown to all players.
E15:
Half-loaded building: with streaming on, a client receives parts gradually and may stream them out again.
- Set the building's Model.ModelStreamingMode = Atomic. The model then streams in and out as a whole, with all descendants together.
- In the LocalScript, wait for the model with WaitForChild, never index it directly, and handle streaming out (react to ChildAdded/ChildRemoved or use CollectionService tag signals).
Always-present scoreboard:
- Set ModelStreamingMode = Persistent. The model is sent at join and never streams out. Use PersistentPerPlayer with Model:AddPersistentPlayer(player) if only some players need it.
- Set these modes in Studio or from server scripts, not LocalScripts.
- Clients still need WaitForChild at startup, because persistent models arrive shortly after join.
Related APIs:
- Player:RequestStreamAroundAsync(position, timeout), called on the server, preloads an area before a teleport or cutscene.
- Workspace StreamingMinRadius/StreamingTargetRadius and StreamOutBehavior tune the radius.
Trade-offs:
- Atomic: a large model arrives later and all at once, so the client may wait longer before it appears.
- Persistent: always uses client memory and bandwidth, and reduces the benefit of streaming, which matters on low-end mobile. Use it only for small essentials, and turn a big building into Atomic, not Persistent.
E16:
Aim direction: yes, switch it to UnreliableRemoteEvent.
- It is continuous, high-frequency data where only the latest value matters, so a dropped or out-of-order packet is harmless. The next update replaces it.
- A reliable event at 30 Hz queues and resends lost packets, which adds latency and can delay your other remotes.
Hit reports: no, keep them on RemoteEvent. A hit must arrive exactly once, and an unreliable event can silently drop or reorder it. Validate hits on the server either way (rate, distance, line of sight, cooldown).
Limits:
- UnreliableRemoteEvent payloads over about 1,000 bytes (after encoding) are dropped, so keep messages to a few numbers or a packed buffer.
- Delivery is not guaranteed and not ordered. Excess traffic over the rate is dropped, not delayed.
- Client-to-server traffic is rate-limited per client and shared across remotes of the same type (about 500 requests/s in the docs).
- Make the server tolerate gaps, and throttle and sanity-check incoming aim data. Consider sending at 20 Hz, or only when the direction changes.
(Vault: RemoteEvents RemoteFunctions and Unreliable Remotes)
E17:
```lua
-- 2 + 4*3 = 14 bytes
local function pack(id: number, pos: Vector3): buffer
  local b = buffer.create(14)
  buffer.writeu16(b, 0, id)
  buffer.writef32(b, 2, pos.X)
  buffer.writef32(b, 6, pos.Y)
  buffer.writef32(b, 10, pos.Z)
  return b
end
local function unpack(b: buffer)
  if typeof(b) ~= "buffer" or buffer.len(b) ~= 14 then return nil end
  local id = buffer.readu16(b, 0)
  local pos = Vector3.new(buffer.readf32(b, 2), buffer.readf32(b, 6), buffer.readf32(b, 10))
  return id, pos
end
-- server: ProjectileUpdate:FireAllClients(pack(id, part.Position))
-- client: ProjectileUpdate.OnClientEvent:Connect(function(b) local id, pos = unpack(b) ... end)
```
Buffer rules relied on:
- buffer.create(n) has a fixed size and is zero-filled. It never grows.
- Offsets are zero-based byte offsets: write(buf, offset, value).
- Reading or writing past the end throws an error. Validate buffer.len before reading untrusted data, especially from clients.
- writeu16 wraps or truncates values outside 0-65535, and f32 loses precision compared with Luau's f64 numbers.
- Values are little-endian. Read with the same layout and order you wrote.
- Buffers are sent through remotes as compact binary, well under the ~1,000-byte unreliable limit.
- To store a buffer in a DataStore, base64 it first.
E18:
Unanchored assemblies are simulated by a network owner: either the server or one client. The engine assigns ownership automatically, usually to the nearest player. Lag for the driver: ownership flips between server and clients, or the server owns the cart. The driver's inputs then make a round trip to the server, and the cart stutters.
Fix:
- When a player sits in the VehicleSeat (Occupant changes), the server calls cartRoot:SetNetworkOwner(player). Ownership is per assembly, so call it on any part of the welded assembly.
- When the seat empties, call SetNetworkOwnershipAuto(), or SetNetworkOwner(nil) to keep it on the server.
- Check part:CanSetNetworkOwnership() first. It returns false plus a reason for anchored assemblies.
Kill brick oddities: while a client owns the cart, that client's physics decides where the cart parts are. Touched events on the server are based on replicated, delayed positions, and the client can spoof them. Cart parts (not character parts) also fire Touched.
- In the handler, resolve hit to a character with Players:GetPlayerFromCharacter(hit.Parent), and ignore cart parts.
- Add a server distance or sanity check before killing.
- Don't trust Touched from client-owned assemblies for anything important.
(Vault: Network Ownership)

According to the vault's 2025-2026 changes note (from Roblox DevForum posts):

E20:
The new properties are ExcludeInstances and IncludeInstances, on both RaycastParams and OverlapParams.
- They replace the single FilterDescendantsInstances list plus a FilterType switch. Instead, you get two lists that work at the same time, each covering descendants.
- IncludeInstances = nil means everything is a candidate. {} means nothing is.
- Anything in ExcludeInstances is always skipped, and exclude wins when an instance is in both lists.
- The old FilterDescendantsInstances/FilterType still works but is documented as superseded. Don't mix the two styles on one params object.
- Other filters still apply: CollisionGroup, RespectCanCollide, and parts with CanQuery = false.
```lua
local params = RaycastParams.new()
params.IncludeInstances = {workspace.Map}
params.ExcludeInstances = {workspace.Map.Glass}
local result = workspace:Raycast(origin, direction, params)
```
Before this change you could pick only Include or Exclude, so this "inside Map but not Glass" case needed a collision group or a manual re-cast. (Vault: Raycasts Shapecasts and Spatial Queries)

E22:
On 2026-01-14 Roblox renamed 46 yielding methods so their names end in Async. This makes it clear that they yield.
- Player:LoadCharacter() became Player:LoadCharacterAsync().
- MarketplaceService:GetProductInfo() became GetProductInfoAsync().
- Others follow the same pattern; for example, BadgeService:AwardBadge became AwardBadgeAsync.
The old names are deprecated for information only. They behave exactly the same, have no announced removal date, and script analysis simply flags them. WaitForChild and InvokeServer/InvokeClient were not renamed.
No urgent rewrite is needed: existing code keeps working. Use the Async names in new code, and switch old calls over gradually, e.g. with find-and-replace when you touch a file. Keep the pcall wrappers, since these calls still yield and can fail. (Vault: Engine and API Changes 2025-2026)
E23:
The vault only covers ProcessReceipt, not BindReceiptHandler. This answer comes from general knowledge, so verify it against the current API docs.
Concept:
- BindReceiptHandler lets each script register a handler for its own developer product ids, instead of one global ProcessReceipt callback. With ProcessReceipt, only the last assignment wins, so two scripts that both set it break each other.
- The handler receives the same receiptInfo as ProcessReceipt (PlayerId, ProductId, PurchaseId, CurrencySpent, ...).
- It must return Enum.ProductPurchaseDecision.PurchaseGranted only after the grant is durably saved, and NotProcessedYet otherwise. Roblox then retries the receipt later.
- Don't also assign ProcessReceipt for the same products. Use one style per experience, or make sure the products don't overlap.
Rules that are the same as ProcessReceipt:
- Be idempotent: record PurchaseId with the grant, so a retried receipt doesn't grant twice.
- If the player is not in the server, return NotProcessedYet.
- Never yield forever.
```lua
local MPS = game:GetService("MarketplaceService")
MPS:BindReceiptHandler(GEMS_100, function(receipt) -- verify exact signature in docs
  local player = game.Players:GetPlayerByUserId(receipt.PlayerId)
  if not player then return Enum.ProductPurchaseDecision.NotProcessedYet end
  local ok = Data.grantOnce(player, receipt.PurchaseId, function(d) d.Gems += 100 end) -- saves
  return ok and Enum.ProductPurchaseDecision.PurchaseGranted or Enum.ProductPurchaseDecision.NotProcessedYet
end)
```
E24:
Luau added these to the math library in 2025:
- math.lerp(a: number, b: number, t: number): number. Returns a + (b - a) * t, with exact endpoints. t is not clamped.
- math.map(x: number, inMin: number, inMax: number, outMin: number, outMax: number): number. Remaps x linearly from one range to the other. It is not clamped either, so use math.clamp on the result if needed.
- math.isnan(x), math.isinf(x) and math.isfinite(x). These replace the x ~= x trick; note that x == math.nan is always false.
The vault also lists newer constants: math.tau, math.e, math.phi, math.sqrt2 and math.nan. Check that your Studio version supports them before relying on them.
Existing helpers include math.clamp, math.sign, math.round (rounds half away from zero) and math.noise.
Example: local hpBarFill = math.map(hp, 0, maxHp, 0, 1).
